lead_with.title: Complement, not compete
lead_with.text: Atera, Xenium and Visium image and read tissue in place. **SLACS pulls out the exact cells or regions** seen on the slide for deep downstream sequencing. Pitch Meteor as the step **after imaging** and **before Psomagen's sequencing**.

lead_with.text: Psomagen says it is the only US provider covering NGS, Sanger, single-cell, proteomics, DTC and microbial work. Spatially-resolved cell sorting would be a **differentiated add-on** for its pharma and academic clients.

company.text: Psomagen (Rockville, MD) is the US subsidiary of Korean genomics group Macrogen; it was Macrogen Corp until July 2019 and has been listed on KOSDAQ since 2020. It sells sequencing and multi-omics services to academia, government and pharma: genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, metagenomics, single-cell, spatial (10x Visium HD, Xenium, Atera), Olink proteomics, long-read (PacBio, Nanopore), bioinformatics and CLIA clinical services. It also runs direct-to-consumer genetic testing. Moderna has been a customer since 2014. In June 2026 it obtained **New York State clinical laboratory certification**. In April 2026 Macrogen and Psomagen committed to deploy multiple **10x Atera** instruments — the first global service provider to do so.

financials.text: **2025 revenue:** US$41.6M (+30% vs US$32.0M in 2024) — record. **2025 operating result:** Consolidated loss US$1.5M (down ~60%); first standalone operating profit. **Q1 2026 revenue:** US$8.76M (+12.4%) — best Q1 ever. **H1 2026:** Revenue US$16.2M; operating profit US$93K (vs loss of US$530K in H1 2025). **Cash (Mar 31, 2026):** US$6.7M; no external funding raised since the 2020 listing. Listed on KOSDAQ (950200). Growth drivers: large NGS projects for US government agencies and the Michael J. Fox Foundation, DTC testing, cost cuts and AI-assisted analysis. Partial stake in subsidiary KEAN Health sold in 2026. Cash is tight — expect interest in revenue-share or low-capex partnership models rather than big equipment buys.

industry.title: Atera raises the spatial bar
industry.text: 10x Genomics launched **Atera** in 2026 for whole-transcriptome spatial at subcellular resolution and scale; trade press says it puts pressure on other spatial players. Service labs like Macrogen/Psomagen are adopting it first.

industry.title: From imaging to isolation
industry.text: As spatial imaging scales, the next question is how to go deeper on the cells it finds — full transcriptome, genome or proteome of rare cells. That is the gap SLACS addresses.

industry.title: Pharma demand
industry.text: Psomagen reports rising pharma revenue and proteomics orders from drug developers — the translational and biomarker users Meteor targets too.

talking_points: Congratulations on Atera — what are your first clients asking to do **after** they see the spatial map?
When a client finds a rare cell population on Xenium or Atera, how do they get deeper data on those exact cells today?
Would a spatially-resolved cell sorting service (SLACS) fit next to your spatial and single-cell lines — as a referral, a pilot or a co-branded service?
Which of your client groups — pharma biomarker teams, NIH-funded labs, clinical — would value this first?
Could we run a joint pilot or webinar: imaging on Atera at Psomagen, cell recovery with SLACS, sequencing back at Psomagen?
How does Macrogen in Korea decide on new platforms — is that a parallel conversation in Seoul?
